html:
Xenophon was an Athenian soldier, historian and pupil of Socrates, who lived from about 430 to 354 BCE.

In 401 BCE he joined a Greek mercenary army hired by the Persian prince Cyrus the Younger, who was trying to take the throne from his brother. Cyrus was killed at the Battle of Cunaxa near Babylon, and the Greek generals were then murdered at a parley. Xenophon was one of the new leaders chosen by the soldiers, and he helped lead the Ten Thousand north through the mountains to the Black Sea. When they saw it they shouted "The sea! The sea!" His account, the Anabasis, showed how far a Greek army could march inside the Persian Empire.

He later served Sparta and fought against Athens in the Corinthian War, and Athens exiled him. He spent years on an estate near Olympia, writing. His works include:

  • the Hellenica, a history of Greece that picks up where Thucydides stops
  • the Memorabilia, memories of Socrates
  • the Cyropaedia, a novel about the education of Cyrus the Great
  • books on horses, hunting and running an estate
sum: Xenophon was an Athenian soldier, historian and pupil of Socrates, who lived from about 430 to 354 BCE.
